title: Pool Maintenance Software 2026: Chem Logs, Checklists & Cost
description: Pool maintenance software compared: which tools log readings, calculate dosing, enforce checklists and email service reports, and what each costs.
h1: Pool maintenance software: chemical logs, checklists and service reports compared
body:
"Pool maintenance software" (or pool management software) is the part of a pool service app your techs touch at every stop: log the water readings, get a dose, tick off the checklist, snap photos, and send the customer a service report before driving to the next pool. Some tools also track equipment per pool and schedule filter and salt cell cleans for you. Below is what six pool-focused tools publish about those maintenance-record features, and what each costs. Everything comes from the vendors' own pricing and feature pages, checked 2026-11-13; anything a vendor doesn't publish is marked unknown. For routing and dispatch, see pool route software and pool service scheduling software; for the overall picture, see best pool service software and the pool service hub.

1. Skimmer: checklists and service emails on the entry plan

Skimmer's Getting Started plan ($1 per serviced location, starts at $49/mo, for 0–49 pools) already includes readings and dosages, service checklists, service reports and emails, a customer portal and 5 photos per visit. Scaling Up ($2 per serviced location, starts at $98/mo, for 50–1,000 pools) adds the LSI & dosing calculator powered by Orenda, LaMotte integration, required checklist items, recurring work orders and 20 photos per visit. Techs and admins are unlimited on both plans, and the app works offline and syncs later. New users can try Scaling Up free for one month (promo terms on Skimmer's page) (Skimmer pricing). Details: Skimmer pricing explained. {{aff:skimmer|See Skimmer plans}}

2. Pool Brain: guided workflows that adapt to the equipment

Pool Brain is built around enforcing the visit: its guided workflows are meant to stop techs skipping steps, and workflows change with the equipment you record (its example: no salt cell means no salt reading is required; a cartridge filter removes the backwash option). Dosing is filled in from the tech's readings, chemical cost is tracked down to the body of water, and filter and salt cell clean jobs are created automatically. Customers get a proof-of-service email with labeled pictures when the stop is done. Pricing is one plan: $50/mo base with unlimited office users plus $65/mo per active field technician (its calculator shows 5 techs at $375/mo) (features, pricing). See Pool Brain. {{aff:poolbrain|Visit Pool Brain}}

3. Pool Office Manager: the most detailed chemistry log we found

Pool Office Manager (POM) lists the readings it captures per visit (pH, chlorine, alkalinity, calcium, cyanuric acid, salt, phosphorus and more), shows each next to the previous visit's value, and calculates LSI and dosing from the gallons stored for each body of water. Equipment (pump, filter, heater, cleaner, salt system, sanitizer) is stored per body of water, pictures are unlimited, and inventory is deducted as techs use it. It's $125/mo for the first user and $25/mo per additional active user, month to month; add-ons are QuickBooks Online sync (+$25/mo), customer texting (from $10/mo) and video storage (+$25/mo). 30-day free trial (POM pricing). See Pool Office Manager. {{aff:poolofficemanager|Visit Pool Office Manager}}

4. UpBuoy: free for up to 3 pools, photo-verified reports

UpBuoy's homepage lists service reports with an LSI calculator and smart dosing, time-stamped and geo-tagged before and after photos, and AI-written service summaries sent to customers. The Essential plan is free for up to 3 locations (technician app, basic scheduling and routing, customer management); Professional is $3 per serviced location per month with a $99 minimum and adds work orders, the customer portal, route optimization and advanced reporting. Paid plans carry a 30-day money-back guarantee (UpBuoy pricing). Checklist features aren't described on the pages we checked. See UpBuoy. {{aff:upbuoy|Visit UpBuoy}}

5. Paythepoolman: low per-tech price, maintenance extras via add-on

Paythepoolman is $50/mo plus $15/mo per technician with no per-pool charge or contract. Its feature list includes Orenda and LaMotte SpinTouch, an equipment log, a shopping list, filter and salt cell cleanings that come due on their own, and chemical cost per dose in its financial records. Customers see service photos and history in the branded Pool Junction app, which is a $25/mo add-on for the whole company. 30-day free trial; the homepage also showed an 80%-off-for-3-months promo code on 2026-11-13 (Paythepoolman). See Paythepoolman. {{aff:paythepoolman|Visit Paythepoolman}}

6. GorillaDesk: checklists and chemical records for mixed pool and pest routes

GorillaDesk isn't pool-only, but its pool page lists chemical use records (material tracking and reporting is on Basic), pool maintenance checklists, notes and attachments. Pricing is per route with unlimited users: Basic $49/mo, Pro $99/mo, Growth $149/mo for one route, month to month, 14-day free trial with no card. Water-chemistry readings, dosing and customer service reports aren't described on the pages we checked, so they're marked unknown (GorillaDesk pool, pricing). Full breakdown: GorillaDesk pricing. {{aff:gorilladesk|Visit GorillaDesk}}

How to choose pool maintenance software

  • Decide what a "complete" visit means. If you want techs blocked from skipping steps, look at Pool Brain's guided workflows or Skimmer's required checklist items (Scaling Up).
  • Check which readings are logged. POM publishes its reading list; for others, open a trial and confirm the readings you test (CYA, salt, phosphates) have fields.
  • Check where dosing lives. Skimmer's Orenda LSI & dosing calculator is on Scaling Up, not Getting Started; Pool Brain, POM and UpBuoy describe dosing without a plan split.
  • Count photo limits. Skimmer caps photos per visit by plan (5, 20 or 30); POM says unlimited.
  • Look at what the customer sees. A service email after each stop is included with Skimmer, Pool Brain and POM; Paythepoolman's customer view is the $25/mo Pool Junction add-on.
  • Test on a real route. Run a week of real stops in the trial. Our software buying checklist lists what to test.

faq: Software pool techs use at each stop to record water readings and chemicals added, work a checklist, take photos and send the customer a service report, usually alongside routing and billing. Skimmer, Pool Brain, Pool Office Manager and UpBuoy all list readings with dosing help and customer service reports on their own pages (checked 2026-11-13).
Which pool software calculates chemical dosing?

Skimmer (LSI & dosing calculator powered by Orenda, on Scaling Up), Pool Brain (dosing auto-calculated from tech readings), Pool Office Manager (LSI and dosing from each body of water's gallons) and UpBuoy (LSI calculator and smart dosing) say so on their pricing or feature pages. Paythepoolman lists Orenda and LaMotte SpinTouch.
Is there free pool maintenance software?
UpBuoy's Essential plan is free for up to 3 locations. Its paid Professional plan is $3 per serviced location per month with a $99 minimum. None of the other pool tools here publish a free plan.
How much does pool maintenance software cost for one tech?

At list prices for 1 tech with 60 pools: GorillaDesk Basic $49/mo, Paythepoolman $65/mo, Pool Brain $115/mo by its formula, Skimmer Scaling Up $120/mo, Pool Office Manager $125/mo and UpBuoy Professional $180/mo. Add-ons, texting and card fees are extra (checked 2026-11-13).
Which pool software sends a service report to the customer after each visit?

Skimmer (service reports and emails on every plan), Pool Brain (automatic proof of service emails, optional per customer), Pool Office Manager (customizable service reports and post-service notices by email or text) and UpBuoy (service summaries with photos). Paythepoolman shows service history and photos in its Pool Junction customer app, a $25/mo add-on.
